proposals.observation: The Daily Blog Post workflow failed at 14:12 on 27 August. There is exactly one post queued and 47 published. The content pipeline has stalled: no new post shipped in the window, and two consecutive CI failures (Daily Blog Post + Funnel-Hack Digest) mean Joel is losing compounding organic reach on the blog's best-performing question-format titles. The cursor commit ("chore(state): update quiz-last-seen cursor") is the only code change in 24 hours, which confirms the failure was not caught and resolved before the next run.
proposals.proposal: Investigate and fix the Daily Blog Post workflow so the queued post publishes today. The .github/workflows path is safety-blocked for Fred, so this is flagged for Joel to action directly. Joel should open the failed run log in GitHub Actions, identify whether the failure is an API timeout, a missing secret, or a schema mismatch with the content frontmatter, and apply the minimal fix. Once the workflow passes, the queued post goes live and the Funnel-Hack Digest run (which likely depends on published content) can be retriggered. This is the single highest-leverage 15 minutes Joel can spend today: every day the pipeline is down is a day the question-format posts stop compounding in search.

proposals.impact: converts best-performing automation's open rate into discovery calls
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has a 66.67% open rate across 12 sends — the strongest open rate of the three active automations, outperforming Money Worship by 29 percentage points. That open rate means subscribers in this segment are reading. Despite that, there is no data suggesting those opens are converting to any next step. The Money Vigilance profile (careful, anxious, rule-following around money) maps closely to the ICP: earners who do everything "right" on paper but still don't build. This segment deserves a sharper call to action inside the sequence.
proposals.proposal: Add a single direct call to action to the final email in the Money Vigilance sequence, pointing to Joel's discovery call booking page. The current sequence almost certainly closes without asking the reader to do anything concrete. Given the open rate, the audience is warm. A plain, grounded sentence that names the specific tension (knowing the rules, still not moving) will outperform any generic "book a call" line. The change is one sentence added to the bottom of the final email before the sign-off.
proposals.current_text: If any of this resonates, I'd love to hear from you.
proposals.new_text: If you've spent years doing the sensible thing with money and still feel like you're watching from behind glass, that's exactly what the first conversation is for. You can book a free 30-minute call with me here: [BOOKING_LINK]

proposals.impact: reduces zero-start drop-off on quiz intro screen
proposals.observation: In the 48-hour quiz window, there was one session and zero starts. The single visitor loaded the intro screen and left. That is a 0% start rate on the one piece of interactive content designed to qualify leads and feed the three email automations. The intro screen is the only thing standing between a visitor and the quiz. If the copy on that screen does not give a reason specific enough to continue, people with a short attention span and mild scepticism — the ICP exactly — will close the tab.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro screen's opening paragraph to replace any generic framing with something concrete and specific to Joel's story, so a first-time visitor understands in under ten seconds why this quiz is different from a personality test. The goal is to raise the start rate from 0% toward something measurable. One paragraph swap, no structural changes to the quiz itself.
proposals.current_text: Find out your money personality type and discover how your relationship with money might be holding you back.
proposals.new_text: When I was earning good money and still couldn't tell you where it went, I didn't have a budgeting problem. I had a pattern I hadn't looked at yet. This four-minute quiz identifies which of three research-backed money patterns is shaping your decisions right now. Joel Smith, MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner.
